questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get out of my comfort and try something completely different from what I am used to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many great experiences! I did not find the academic part of it that interesting, but I still learned some interesting things and met some great people. Traveling Japan, exploring Tokyo and getting new friends were the best parts.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got a mail with the important information from the university, so it was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went and got information about the courses from another students. They also had some introducing activities and international student cafés.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I lost a lottery for campus housing, but then I applied to something else, which I ended up getting and liked a lot. As a dane, the prices for rent are also fine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It can be nice to not have your whole life on campus. Where I lived, there were people who were not students, which I appreciated because of the different kinds of people I got to meet.
You should apply for a social place, because otherwise it get pretty isolating, is my impression. Either a place with many social activities or where you get meet people in a common room. I met some of my best friends at my sharehouse.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I made some great friends and got to explore another part of the city. The room itself was small and kind of ugly, but that just motivated me to leave it:)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Straightforward, but very long.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Too long. So much paper work. Be prepared for that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The website (though difficult to use) and asking on e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all of them. Two of them I lost in a lottery, but it was with a popular teacher.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a lot of paperwork. Do the language test as early as possible so you don't miss the deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting courses, but not always what I expected. Not the highest academic level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them were not that high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. More attendance and active participation. The use of AI was evident.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 8 different courses in the school of social sciences - learned about anthropology, health and human rights, monozukuri culture etc.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The language test (TOEFL, in my instance). Insurances. And remember the national health insurance in Japan, too.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruit is expensive. But food in general is so cheap and delicious.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use them, but they seemed fine.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not use it a lot. But I think we had some cafes for international students, and some sport activities and gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible. But also explore Tokyo: the izakayas and bars, onsen/sentos (public baths), thrift stores, museums, cafés and kissatans, parks, arcades, etc. etc. There is so much to explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fine, a lot of it is intuitive. Just be respectful and you will be fine. Don't talk on your phone on the train, learn to say thank you and sorry in Japanese... etc.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I did not make many Japanese friends to be honest. But you can meet people in classes. And you can become part of the clubs/circles.
It was easier for me to make international friends as we were in the same situation, and many people are ready to explore the city together if you ask.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier. But it is manageable, especially if you learn the basic phrases.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Good food and all the stuff I already mentioned.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Again, be prepared for the paper work. Do the language test as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making good friends from around the world and getting to explore Tokyo and Japan in general. Seeing the nature. Getting confidence knowing you can travel to Japan for five months and be fine.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it! Even though there is a lot of paperwork, it has been a life changing experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
